title: Answer: information, like causation, is defined against what does not happen, and comes in types

statements.text: Causal emergence uses information in the sense of information theory and ties it to causation. Both are defined with respect to what does not exist: causation relies on counterfactuals, information theory on unsent signals. A macroscale can raise causal information the way a code uses more of a channel's capacity. Information also comes in types, redundant, unique and synergistic, and a macroscale can convert information from one type to another with no change but the scale of the model, which is how the framework reads emergence.
statements.scope: When the map is better than the territory (2016) and Emergence as the conversion of information (2021)

sources.quote: There is a natural, but unremarked upon, connection between causation and information theory.
Both causation and information are defined in respect to the nonexistent: causation relies on counterfactual statements, and information theory on unsent signals.
information can be converted from one type to another, with no change except for what scale the system is being modeled at
